raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The `EagerRunner` builds one fixed-size input registry at startup. Its token-axis slots (`input_ids`, `positions`, `out_cache_loc` int64 and `mrope_positions` 3 x int64: 48 bytes per token) are sized to `max(max_total_num_tokens, chunked_prefill_size)`, the whole KV pool. An eager pass carries one prefill batch, bounded by the chunk / `max_prefill_tokens`, or a decode-shaped batch, so almost all of that memory is never written. The waste scales with the KV pool: a small model on a large GPU has a multi-million-token pool and wastes hundreds of MB of device memory that activations and CUDA graphs could use.

## Modifications

- `model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py`:
  - The registry is sized by the prefill limit: `max(chunked_prefill_size (or the PP dynamic-chunking ceiling), min(max_total_num_tokens, max_prefill_tokens), max_bs * tokens_per_req)`. It is never larger than before.
  - `load_batch` regrows it when a batch is larger (e.g. chunked prefill disabled and a long prompt). The regrown registry is the next power of two, capped at the old pool-based size, and is built outside the process-wide input-buffer pool. The first regrow does not free the startup registry: it stays in that pool, whose slots the CUDA-graph runners share. Each later regrow frees the previous regrown registry.
- `model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py`: `build_eager_registry(share_pool=...)` (default `True`, unchanged for every existing caller).
- Test: `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_eager_runner_input_registry.py` (CPU) covers four cases:
  - a large pool does not size the registry;
  - a small pool keeps the chunk ceiling;
  - a larger batch regrows the registry, and smaller batches reuse it;
  - a regrow is capped at the old size and is not kept in the shared pool.

The values copied into the slots and the kernels are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the same RTX PRO 6000, main vs this PR: greedy outputs of 7 prompts (single, repeated twice, and batched) are **token-identical**, and main is repeat-identical in this config. With prefill forced through the eager runner and the regrow path exercised (`--enable-deterministic-inference --chunked-prefill-size -1 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 512`; the server logs `Eager input registry: 14408 tokens > 4096; regrowing to 16384.`), outputs are again token-identical to main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Device memory after startup, same GPU (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, 300 W), `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-deterministic-inference`. The KV pool here is 6,979,341 tokens:

| | main `8d4e1ce4c7` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPU memory used after startup | 87,716 MiB | 87,396 MiB (**−320 MiB**) |
| Free after CUDA-graph capture | 9.42 GB | 9.73 GB |
| KV cache tokens | 6,979,341 | 6,979,341 |

Forced-eager config above (KV pool 7,284,335 tokens), same GPU: 91,024 MiB used on main vs 90,688 MiB with this PR (−336 MiB), and 6.19 vs 6.52 GB free after CUDA-graph capture.

The saving is freed after the KV pool is sized, so it is runtime headroom, not KV capacity, and it scales with the pool size: 48 B x (pool − prefill ceiling). With `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` on the same GPU, the pool is only 140,928 tokens, so the expected saving is 48 B x (140,928 − 16,384) = 6.0 MB, which this free-memory reading does not resolve (11.18 GB on main vs 11.20 GB with this PR after CUDA-graph capture, one run each, measured on an earlier commit of this PR with the same initial sizing; only the regrow path changed since). No saving is claimed for that model, and no speed change is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (pre-commit `--all-files` clean)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test_eager_runner_input_registry.py`, CPU-registered)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (token-identical gate and memory table above; no speed claim)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""EagerRunner input registry sizing.
+
+The token-axis input slots (input_ids, positions, out_cache_loc, ...) hold one
+eager batch: they are sized by the prefill limit rather than the KV pool, and a
+larger batch regrows them, outside the shared input-buffer pool and never above
+the pool-based size used before.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.cuda_graph_buffer_registry import (
+    CudaGraphBufferRegistry,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.input_buffers import _forward_input_buffer_pool
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner import eager_runner as eager_runner_module
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner.eager_runner import EagerRunner
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_info import SpeculativeAlgorithm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+CHUNK = 4096
+MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS = 16384
+
+
+class TestEagerRunnerInputRegistry(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        override = get_context().override_server_args(
+            chunked_prefill_size=CHUNK, max_prefill_tokens=MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS
+        )
+        override.install()
+        self.addCleanup(override.restore)
+        no_dllm = mock.patch.object(
+            eager_runner_module.DllmConfig, "from_server_args", return_value=None
+        )
+        no_dllm.start()
+        self.addCleanup(no_dllm.stop)
+
+    def _runner(self, max_total_num_tokens: int) -> EagerRunner:
+        model_runner = SimpleNamespace(
+            device="cpu",
+            is_draft_worker=False,
+            spec_algorithm=SpeculativeAlgorithm.NONE,
+            server_args=None,
+            max_running_requests=8,
+            max_total_num_tokens=max_total_num_tokens,
+            model_config=SimpleNamespace(
+                is_encoder_decoder=False, hf_config=SimpleNamespace()
+            ),
+        )
+        return EagerRunner(model_runner, run_warmup=False)
+
+    def _input_ids_numel(self, runner: EagerRunner) -> int:
+        return runner._eager_registry.get_slot("input_ids").buffer.numel()
+
+    def test_large_kv_pool_does_not_size_the_registry(self):
+        runner = self._runner(max_total_num_tokens=10_000_000)
+        self.assertEqual(runner._eager_registry.max_num_tokens, MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS)
+        self.assertEqual(self._input_ids_numel(runner), MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS)
+
+    def test_small_kv_pool_keeps_the_chunk_ceiling(self):
+        runner = self._runner(max_total_num_tokens=1000)
+        self.assertEqual(runner._eager_registry.max_num_tokens, CHUNK)
+
+    def test_larger_batch_regrows_the_registry(self):
+        runner = self._runner(max_total_num_tokens=10_000_000)
+        batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            batch_size=1,
+            input_ids=torch.zeros(MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS + 1, dtype=torch.int64),
+            input_embeds=None,
+        )
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(CudaGraphBufferRegistry, "fill_from") as fill_from,
+            mock.patch.object(CudaGraphBufferRegistry, "extract_buffer"),
+        ):
+            runner.load_batch(batch)
+            grown = runner._eager_registry
+            self.assertEqual(grown.max_num_tokens, 2 * MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS)
+            self.assertEqual(self._input_ids_numel(runner), 2 * MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                fill_from.call_args.kwargs["raw_num_tokens"], MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS + 1
+            )
+
+            batch.input_ids = torch.zeros(CHUNK, dtype=torch.int64)
+            runner.load_batch(batch)
+            self.assertIs(runner._eager_registry, grown)
+
+    def test_regrow_is_capped_and_not_pooled(self):
+        pool_tokens = 20_000
+        runner = self._runner(max_total_num_tokens=pool_tokens)
+        batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            batch_size=1,
+            input_ids=torch.zeros(MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS + 1, dtype=torch.int64),
+            input_embeds=None,
+        )
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(CudaGraphBufferRegistry, "fill_from"),
+            mock.patch.object(CudaGraphBufferRegistry, "extract_buffer"),
+        ):
+            runner.load_batch(batch)
+        # The next power of two (32,768) would exceed the old pool-based size.
+        self.assertEqual(runner._eager_registry.max_num_tokens, pool_tokens)
+        grown = runner._eager_registry.get_slot("input_ids").buffer
+        pooled = {
+            b.untyped_storage().data_ptr() for b in _forward_input_buffer_pool.values()
+        }
+        self.assertNotIn(grown.untyped_storage().data_ptr(), pooled)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
